skill.name: creating-claude-agents
skill.description: Guides creation and improvement of Claude Code agents through frontmatter rules, persona design, tool permissions, model selection, templates, validation, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Design focused Claude Code agents with valid structure, clear roles, appropriate models, and minimal tool access.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: All 105 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documentation links, and unrelated prose. Semantic review identified overbroad guidance that can make agents inherit every parent tool.

remediation.issue: The guide recommends omitting allowed-tools to inherit every parent tool.
remediation.suggestion: Remove this permission-denied workaround and require explicit, task-specific tool lists. Explain any unavoidable broad access and require user confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Tool Inheritance Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends omitting allowed-tools to inherit every parent tool and repeats this as a permission fix. Generated agents may receive unnecessary shell, filesystem, or network access.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited passages explicitly describe unrestricted inheritance and recommend it after permission denial. Other sections acknowledge least privilege, confirming the security tradeoff is relevant.

content.value_statement: Claude Code agent files require precise frontmatter, tool permissions, personas, and structure. This skill provides templates, validation rules, examples, and troubleshooting guidance for reliable agent creation.
actual_capabilities: Explains required and optional Claude Code agent frontmatter fields.
Provides minimal and comprehensive agent file templates.
Compares agent, skill, and slash command use cases.
Guides model selection among sonnet, opus, haiku, and inherit.
Provides validation checklists and troubleshooting steps for activation, schema, and tool issues.
Shows least-privilege tool patterns, including restricted Bash commands.
limitations: Does not run schema validation or test generated agents automatically.
References an external schema and a developer-specific local path that may be unavailable.
Uses model names and tool conventions that may change across Claude Code versions.
Examples target Claude Code agents and may require adaptation for Codex or other systems.

use_cases.title: Create a Review Agent
use_cases.description: Build a focused code review agent with clear activation language, a review process, and minimal read-only tools.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Agents
use_cases.description: Define consistent names, frontmatter, personas, permissions, models, and validation checks across a shared agent library.

use_cases.title: Repair Agent Configuration
use_cases.description: Diagnose activation failures, schema errors, missing tools, and vague responsibilities in existing Claude Code agents.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Minimal Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal Claude Code agent named [name] for [task]. Use only necessary tools and explain each frontmatter choice.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the agent at [path]. Identify schema errors, vague activation language, excess permissions, and missing structure. Propose a corrected version.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Domain Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a specialized [domain] agent for [workflow]. Select a suitable model, define measurable steps, restrict tools, and include realistic examples.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Agent Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit agents in [directory] for naming, schema compliance, overlapping roles, permissions, activation quality, and model fit. Produce prioritized recommendations.

output_examples.input: Create a read-only agent that reviews TypeScript changes for security and maintainability.
output: A focused code reviewer profile with a lowercase, hyphenated name.
Read and search permissions only, with no unrestricted shell access.
A structured review process covering security, quality, and actionable findings.

output_examples.input: Explain why my agent does not activate for database migration reviews.
output: The description is too broad to match database migration requests reliably.
Use explicit activation language covering migration safety, rollback plans, and schema changes.
Verify the file location, frontmatter syntax, name pattern, and model value.

output_examples.input: Choose an agent type and model for rapid formatting checks.
output_examples.output: Use a narrow agent only when repeatable tool-assisted checks are required. The guide recommends haiku for fast, simple validation tasks.

best_practices: Define one measurable responsibility and state when the agent should activate.
Grant only the tools required for the workflow, using restricted command patterns where possible.
Validate frontmatter, test realistic tasks, and include examples for expected behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not combine review, debugging, testing, refactoring, and documentation into one generic agent.
Do not grant unrestricted Bash, write, or network tools without a documented requirement.
Do not rely on vague descriptions, missing personas, or untested examples.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It guides the design of Claude Code agent Markdown files with frontmatter, personas, workflows, permissions, models, examples, and validation checks.

faq.question: Does the skill generate agent files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and templates that Claude, Codex, or a developer can use to create or revise files.

faq.question: Which fields are required?
faq.answer: The guide requires lowercase name and description fields. It also expects an H1 heading and a clear persona in the content.

faq.question: How should tool access be selected?
faq.answer: Choose the smallest explicit tool set that completes the task. Restrict shell commands to specific patterns when shell access is necessary.

faq.question: How does it help choose a model?
faq.answer: It maps sonnet to general work, opus to complex reasoning, haiku to fast checks, and inherit to parent model selection.

faq.question: Can these templates be used with Codex?
faq.answer: The design principles are transferable, but frontmatter fields, tool names, paths, and model settings may need adaptation for Codex.
